evals.name: purchase-event-missing-items
evals.prompt: GA4 purchase events arrive but revenue is 0 and items are empty. Our dev pushes this on the thank-you page: dataLayer.push({event:'purchase', transaction_id: order.id, value: order.total, items: order.lines}). In GTM the GA4 event tag has 'Send Ecommerce data' enabled with data source Data Layer. Preview shows the event firing. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis that the push lacks the ecommerce wrapper object required by the GA4 schema (ecommerce: {transaction_id, value, currency, items}), recommends clearing with ecommerce: null first, provides corrected code, and verification steps in Preview Data Layer tab and DebugView.
assertions: Identifies that transaction_id, value and items must sit inside an 'ecommerce' object for the GA4 tag to read them
Provides corrected dataLayer code including currency and the ecommerce: null reset
Verification steps include checking the Data Layer tab in Preview and GA4 DebugView
States a root cause with a confidence level

evals.name: works-in-preview-not-production-consent
evals.prompt: Google Ads conversions dropped 70% two weeks ago in Germany. In Tag Assistant Preview everything fires fine. We added a Cookiebot banner around that time. Tags look unchanged. Help.
evals.expected_output: Points to consent mode as the cause: default denied in EEA, most users decline or the update call is missing; explains how to verify in Tag Assistant's Consent tab (On-page Default / Update), checks the CMP sends gtag consent update, mentions Consent Initialization trigger and modelling; notes Preview does not bypass consent.
assertions: Names consent mode v2 / the new CMP as the probable cause and explains the mechanism
Describes checking the Consent tab in Tag Assistant for default and update states
Recommends verifying the gtag('consent','update') call and the Consent Initialization trigger
Corrects the assumption that Preview shows production behaviour by explaining consent state is visible there
Includes a test with consent denied and granted in incognito

evals.name: spa-duplicate-pageviews
evals.prompt: Our React site (client-side routing) shows roughly double page_view counts in GA4 after we added a History Change trigger to a GA4 page_view event tag. The Google tag is on Initialization - All Pages. Why double, and how do we fix it without losing SPA pageviews?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the Google tag already sends page_view on load (and enhanced measurement may send history-based page views), so the extra tag duplicates; recommends either disabling the Google tag's automatic page_view / enhanced measurement page changes or removing the custom tag, and verifying counts in Preview and DebugView.
assertions: Identifies the duplicate source: Google tag's automatic page_view plus the History Change tag (and/or enhanced measurement page changes)
Offers a concrete fix that keeps SPA pageviews (one mechanism only)
Includes verification: count page_view fires per route change in Preview and DebugView
Mentions that the first load should not fire the History-based tag

checks.pattern: enhanced measurement|automatic page_view|send a page view
